result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A has a cleaner desktop layout: all eight columns sit on one line, rows are compact with zebra striping and a strong header, and all 12 sailings fit on screen. B does better on rubric item 4 because its routes are bold, but the routes wrap onto two lines, so rows are taller and harder to scan. Neither screenshot shows the viewport meta tag or how the page handles a narrow screen, so both get a neutral 3 on item 3. A also makes the arrival time bold, so it competes with the departure time. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B fits all 12 sailings into a compact desktop table where each route stays on one line, so it is easier to scan and should print better. A makes the route text bold, which keeps departure and route the most prominent information, but routes wrap onto two lines and make the rows tall. B gives the arrival time the same bold weight as the departure, which weakens the hierarchy, and neither screenshot shows how the page handles a narrow phone screen.
